title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (Dec 2026 data) — the January edition, on the SECOND business day
source: EST: ISM's own release-schedule paragraph, read verbatim on 2026-09-05 from the August-2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI report (PRNewswire, dateline Tempe, Ariz., 2026-09-01): 'The full text version of the ISM(R) Manufacturing PMI(R) Report is posted on ISM(R)'s website at www.ismrob.org on the first business day* of every month after 10:00 a.m. ET. The one exception is in January when the report is released on the second business day of the month.' — footnote '*Unless the New York Stock Exchange is closed.' January 2027's business days begin Mon 2027-01-04 (2027-01-01 is a Friday holiday), so the SECOND is Tue 2027-01-05. Note this corrects the rule as recorded on this calendar: the five existing ism-manufacturing entries (2026-09-01, -10-01, -11-02, -12-01, 2027-02-01) all state the cadence as 'the first business day of the month' with NO January exception, because none of them is a January edition — the rule as written would have dated this one 2027-01-04, a day early. The same 2026-09-01 report names its immediate successor verbatim ('the next ISM(R) Manufacturing PMI(R) Report featuring September 2026 data will be released at 10:00 a.m. ET on Thursday, October 1, 2026'), so this date becomes primary-sourced from the December-2026 edition. ismworld.org was probed direct 2026-09-05 and returned a 922-byte Google-reCAPTCHA challenge on its ROB-calendar path and HTTP 404 on its services path, so no 2027 schedule could be read; this is a rule-derived date and nothing more, checked 2026-09-05
notes: DISCOVERED during the ism-services-2027-01-07 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). Fills the same year-boundary gap its services sibling does: this calendar tracked ISM manufacturing monthly through 2026-12-01 and then stopped at the 2026 boundary rather than at any analytical judgement. Filed at impact high to match the five existing manufacturing entries. Note the geometry the two January exceptions produce: manufacturing shifts +1 (first->second business day) and services shifts +1 (third->fourth), so 2027-01-05 -> 2027-01-07 preserves the ordinary two-session gap between the pair even though both dates move. RULE VALIDATED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research: the manufacturing January second-business-day arm, which no sibling in this chain had ever tested, reproduces 5/5 against independently datestamped ISM primaries (2019-01-03, 2021-01-05, 2023-01-04, 2025-01-03 and 2026-01-05 — the Dec-2025 report's dateline reads verbatim 'TEMPE, Ariz., Jan. 5, 2026'), every one of them a day later than the incomplete rule this calendar previously recorded. READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT — but NOT for the reason this note originally gave. The services sibling's placebo verdict was extended to manufacturing here sight-unseen; researching it found that extension too broad in one direction and understated in another. (a) That sibling's 528-session 'other early-month days' control CONTAINED all 132 ISM manufacturing release days, the most elevated early-month cell there is; rebuilt as the 396 sessions carrying neither ISM release, its own ^TNX cell moves from 37.1% vs 30.1% (p=0.142, null) to 37.1% vs 27.0% (p=0.036). (b) Manufacturing SURVIVES the placebo services failed: TLT 37.9% vs 28.0% (p=0.038) and ^TNX 39.4% vs 27.0% (p=0.009), equities flat on baseline. (c) It is disposed of instead by the natural experiment only THIS date makes available — January moves the print off TD1 onto TD2, and pooled bonds show the elevation stays with the slot: TD1 with the release 39.7% (n=242) vs TD1 without it 31.8% (p=0.505); TD2 with it 27.3% vs TD2 without it 26.9% (p=1.000); in January the largest bond cell is TD3 at 54.5%, the one day of that week carrying no ISM release at all. What is well-powered is trading-day position, bonds only (TD1 vs TD>5: ^TNX 39.4% vs 19.6%, p=4.1e-7; TLT 38.6% vs 19.9%, p=2.4e-6), with mechanism deliberately unsourced.
